intro: Two homes with the same purchase price in Columbus and Cleveland may have noticeably different monthly housing costs. Local school district taxes, insurance premiums, association fees and property maintenance can influence how much you actually spend on homeownership.

Our free Ohio mortgage calculator helps you estimate your monthly payment before purchasing a property. Enter your home price, down payment, mortgage interest rate and loan term, then include property taxes and insurance to establish a realistic homebuying budget.

sections.heading: Quick Answer: How Much Is a Mortgage Payment in Ohio?

blocks.markdown:
A $215,000 Ohio home purchased with a 20% down payment and financed through a 30-year mortgage at a 6% fixed annual interest rate would have a monthly principal and interest payment of approximately $1,031.23.

Including illustrative property taxes and insurance produces the following estimate.

This example assumes no private mortgage insurance or association fees. The interest rate, property taxes and insurance premiums are illustrative planning assumptions rather than current statewide averages.

Ohio offers housing opportunities across major metropolitan areas, university communities, suburban developments and smaller rural towns.

According to the [US Census Bureau's Ohio housing statistics](https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/OH/HSD310224), the median value of owner-occupied housing was $214,800 during the 2020–2024 survey period.

Median selected monthly ownership costs among households with mortgages were $1,517, while approximately 67.2% of occupied housing units were owner-occupied.

These historical figures include existing homeowners who may have purchased properties at lower prices or different interest rates.

Housing expenses around Columbus, Cincinnati, Cleveland, Dayton and Toledo can vary considerably. Research recent comparable property sales and investigate local tax obligations before entering a purchase price into the calculator.

sections.heading: How to Use the Ohio Mortgage Calculator

blocks.markdown:
Start by entering the expected purchase price of your property and your available down payment.

Choose a mortgage repayment term and enter the annual interest rate quoted by your lender. If you haven't received a quote, consult [Freddie Mac's mortgage market survey](https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms) for a national reference.

Include annual property taxes, homeowners insurance premiums and monthly association fees. Add private mortgage insurance if required by your conventional financing.

Review the estimated monthly payment breakdown and adjust individual inputs to compare financing arrangements.

The amortization schedule shows how your mortgage balance decreases throughout the repayment period.

Use our national Mortgage Calculator to compare borrowing scenarios outside Ohio.

sections.heading: How Ohio Property Taxes Affect Your Mortgage

blocks.markdown:
Ohio calculates residential property taxes using appraised property values, statutory assessment ratios, applicable tax levies and available credits.

County auditors determine property valuations, while local taxing districts collect revenue to support schools, emergency services and other public functions.

### Ohio residential property assessment ratio

According to the [Ohio Department of Taxation's real property tax guidance](https://tax.ohio.gov/help-center/faqs/real-property-tax-general), real estate is assessed at 35% of its appraised value.

A home appraised at $215,000 would therefore have an assessed value of $75,250.

The 35% assessment ratio determines the value used for taxation. It does not represent the percentage of your home's market value that you pay annually in property taxes.

Actual tax liabilities may differ because of applicable credits, exemptions, special assessments and local levy arrangements.

Obtain the property's latest tax statement from the county auditor or treasurer before establishing your mortgage budget.

### Ohio property reappraisal cycle

Ohio counties conduct full real estate reappraisals every six years, with an interim valuation update three years after each full reappraisal.

The state's [property reappraisal and update schedule](https://tax.ohio.gov/government/real-state) identifies upcoming valuation changes by county.

An increase in appraised property value does not necessarily produce an equivalent percentage increase in your tax bill.

Tax reduction factors and the structure of individual levies can influence the final amount payable.

Ask your county auditor whether an upcoming reappraisal, new levy or other adjustment could affect your future property taxes.

The standard means-tested exemption has an income threshold of $41,000 for the 2026 real property tax year.

Certain applicants qualify under different income or grandfathering provisions.

The exemption is delivered through a tax bill credit calculated using the applicable sheltered home value. It is not a cash payment equal to the exemption amount.

Ohio has also introduced additional property tax relief legislation. Consult the state's [property tax legislation directory](https://tax.ohio.gov/government/real-state/real-property-tax-legislation) for current changes affecting your county.

Ohio homeowners may experience thunderstorms, hail, tornadoes, winter storms and flooding.

Insurance premiums depend on your property's condition, rebuilding cost, construction materials, location and coverage requirements.

Request multiple insurance quotes before completing your purchase.

### Flood and water backup coverage

The [Ohio Department of Insurance](https://insurance.ohio.gov/consumers/homeowner/flood-insurance-information) explains that standard homeowners insurance does not include flood protection.

Properties near rivers, streams and low-lying areas may require separate flood coverage.

Investigate your property's exposure using the [FEMA Flood Map Service Center](https://msc.fema.gov/portal/home).

Homeowners with basements should also discuss sewer backup and sump pump coverage with their insurance agents. These protections may require additional endorsements.

### Mine subsidence insurance

Properties in areas affected by historical underground mining may have additional insurance considerations.

The state's [homeowners insurance guide](https://insurance.ohio.gov/consumers/homeowner/homeowners-insurance-guide) explains specialized coverage options, including mine subsidence protection.

Investigate whether the property is in an affected county and whether coverage is mandatory or optional under applicable rules.

Include all applicable insurance premiums when calculating your total monthly housing expenses.

The Ohio Housing Finance Agency, commonly known as OHFA, offers mortgage financing and purchase assistance through participating lenders.

### OHFA Down Payment Assistance

Current [OHFA homebuyer program guidance](https://ohiohome.org/partners/faqs.aspx) identifies the following assistance options:

For a qualifying $215,000 purchase, conventional assistance would amount to $6,450, while government-backed mortgage assistance would amount to $7,525.

Standard assistance is forgiven after seven years when applicable requirements are satisfied. Selling the property before the forgiveness period ends can require full repayment.

### Ohio Heroes and Grants for Grads

Ohio Heroes provides discounted mortgage rates to qualifying residents in designated public service occupations.

Grants for Grads provides eligible recent graduates with mortgage and purchase assistance. Its forgiveness arrangement generally requires recipients to remain in Ohio for five years.

Next Home provides financing opportunities for qualifying repeat buyers.

Review [OHFA's published mortgage rates](https://ww.ohiohome.org/rates/) and compare financing options with and without assistance. Assistance-based mortgages may have higher interest rates than equivalent loans without assistance.

A shorter mortgage term can substantially reduce your lifetime borrowing costs.

For example, a $172,000 loan financed at 6% would require approximately $1,031.23 monthly in principal and interest over 30 years.

A 15-year repayment period at the same rate would increase the monthly principal and interest payment to approximately $1,451.42.

Although the shorter mortgage requires a higher monthly commitment, it reduces the number of years over which interest accrues.

Use the calculator's amortization schedule to compare both options. Our [Mortgage Extra Payment Calculator](/calculators/mortgage-extra-payment-calculator/) can also help you explore paying additional principal without committing to a shorter contractual repayment period.

sections.heading: Additional Costs of Owning an Ohio Home

blocks.markdown:
Ohio buyers should consider winter heating expenses, roof maintenance, utilities and unexpected repairs.

Older properties may require electrical upgrades, plumbing repairs or basement waterproofing.

Condominium buyers should investigate association reserves and potential special assessments. Rural properties may involve private wells, septic systems and access road maintenance.

Use our [Ohio Paycheck Calculator](/calculators/ohio-paycheck-calculator/) to estimate after-tax income and our [Debt to Income Ratio Calculator](/debt/debt-to-income-ratio-calculator/) to evaluate existing borrowing obligations.

Compare mortgage offers using the [CFPB Loan Estimate guide](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/owning-a-home/loan-estimate/).

Maintain sufficient emergency savings rather than committing your entire cash balance to the down payment.

### How much is a mortgage payment on a $215,000 Ohio home?

With 20% down, a 6% fixed interest rate and a 30-year mortgage, monthly principal and interest would be approximately $1,031.23. Property taxes, insurance and other applicable expenses increase the total housing payment.

### How are Ohio residential property taxes calculated?

Ohio generally assesses real estate at 35% of its appraised value. Applicable local tax rates are applied to assessed value, with adjustments for eligible credits, exemptions and other charges.

### Does Ohio offer down payment assistance?

Yes. OHFA offers qualifying borrowers assistance equal to 3% of the purchase price for conventional mortgages or 3.5% for eligible government-backed loans. Standard assistance has a seven-year forgiveness period, subject to program requirements.
